description.text:
I lead the Backend Platform org within the Developer Experience org.

My org consists of two main groups: Languages & Insights Platform and Internal Developer Platform.

The Languages & Insights Platform group includes Core Python and Core Java teams that create tools, libraries, and best practices to help service authors write high quality, performant, maintainable code in Python and JVM languages. We also have a Developer Insights & Automation team that creates an ecosystem of products that make it easy to understand the quality of our systems and enable teams to quickly and efficiently identify their highest priority maintenance tasks. This group also drives our AI developer tools strategy to bring the latest AI tools to all developers at Yelp.

The Internal Developer Platform group includes Application Observability and Release & Observability teams that build tools for logging, tracing and metrics data collection and dashboard tools for feature teams to understand performance regressions. They also manage our CICD pipelines and code review and release process for backend services. We also have a Developer Environments team that manages our IDEs, tools for local testing, AI code generation tools and paved-path environments for Python and JVM development.

description.text: I work on the Infrastructure as a Service group developing a Java Spring web service to manage Load Balancer devices. I work in PayPal's Core Platform Infrastructure group that is responsible for running PayPal's private cloud. PayPal has one of the largest deployments of OpenStack in production. Specifically, I worked on the Identity (Keystone) and Dashboard (Horizon) services of OpenStack. My role involved working with product management to define requirements, designing, coding and testing product features and working with customers to design solutions for provisioning and maintaining cloud resources. I also worked on defining engineering processes like change management, blueprint design reviews and sprint planning.

I designed, implemented and tested a protocol to dynamically create policies for application delivery controllers attached to a network switch. I was involved from the requirements and prototyping phase until the product was tested and shipped to customers. In this project, I was responsible for driving the design of interaction with other software components, designing to overcome the limitations of the system and aggressive testing to handle all failure scenarios.

I designed and implemented a protocol for network analyzers attached to a switch to control and apply configuration to span traffic to the analytics appliance. I was involved in design reviews for switch and appliance software to produce a unified experience to the end-user. Some of my responsibilities include system design, coding and testing of software, managing project deadlines and expectations, coordinating with other project leads for software integration, coordinating with build and release managers for code commit and troubleshooting with QA and development engineers.

I am involved in talking to customers to understand their topology and requirements and figuring out how best to use our features. This includes PoC demos, presentations and product enhancements to fit customer needs. I do most of my development in C and testing in Python/other scripting languages.

I was a research assistant focusing on parallelizing demand-driven static analysis using Microsoft Phoenix framework. I was a teaching assistant for several undergraduate programming courses. Teaching programming labs, grading and guiding students to solve homework assignments were some of my responsibilities.

I worked on automating the segregation of performance data using TCL scripts. I also wrote test cases and did functional and performance testing on the ASR 1K Edge router. I was responsible for implementing fixes and committing code for feature enhancements.
I was responsible for implementing test suites using SoapUI to test a vendor management tool for the U.S. government. I also worked on SQL to validate the database for various test scenarios.

projects.title: Keystone V3 API with Apache frontend
projects.subtitle: Jun 2016 - Jun 2016

description.text: Implemented upgrade from v2.0 to v3 API versions including PayPal specific customizations. Improved performance by up to 4x by implemented an Apache front-end for the identity service.

Implemented customizations to the dashboard such as management of Virtual Private Cloud (VPC), certification of images for provisioning virtual machines etc. Improved service performance by 10x by modifying API calls based on role privileges.

Implemented a bootstrap protocol to facilitate the automatic creation of SPAN traffic analysis services on a network switch with failure detection and recovery capabilities. The protocol initiates a handshake between the supervisor and line card, recovers the hardware and software specifications of the module and applies configuration to send traffic to the module for analysis.

When load balancers are configured in the datacenter, there is a need to redirect return traffic from the server to the load-balancer appliance for security reasons. Configuring these redirection rules is tedious, error-prone and subject to frequent changes. APBR dynamically creates policies to redirect server return traffic to a load-balancer appliance based on the services configured in the appliance. Further, the algorithm handles errors, updates policies based on changes in service and purges configuration when needed. The user no longer needs to manually create or update any policy configuration on the switch.

Implemented a protocol that allows a network switch to automatically bootstrap, handshake with and configure remote third-party L4-L7 network appliances in the datacenter. Service appliances can dynamically push configuration to the datacenter switch as well as accept configuration from the switch. This simplified provisioning protocol has been shown to reduce the CAPEX and OPEX costs of customers by an order of magnitude.
